# FSM_COS 0.1.0-alpha.7 — Internal Release Evidence Checklist

This is an internal checklist, not consumer documentation. It records required evidence, not a live status report. Always inspect the current `development` HEAD and its workflow runs; do not copy status, percentages, or artifact hashes from an older candidate.

## Candidate and source contract

- Confirm the intended source SHA and declared package version `0.1.0-alpha.7`.
- Review source, public API, tests, and consumer documentation together.
- Confirm every documented behavior is implemented and covered by relevant tests.
- Keep explicit limitations explicit; a staged metadata type is not proof of a complete staged-loading pipeline.
- Confirm the direct dependency set and versions against the project file and package artifact.

## Required CI and package evidence

- [ ] Pack-and-test workflow succeeds on the exact candidate SHA.
- [ ] Source-integration and public-package compatibility jobs succeed on that SHA.
- [ ] CodeQL succeeds on that SHA.
- [ ] Inspect the exact package artifact(s): package ID/version, target framework, dependency metadata, license/readme, XML documentation, intended documentation/assets, and exclusions for maintainer notes.
- [ ] Confirm all packaged local Markdown links resolve within the package and SVG contract checks pass.
- [ ] Confirm the public-feed compatibility build uses the intended public dependency versions.
- [ ] Confirm `publish_nuget` remains skipped and no package was published.

## Documentation and visual evidence

- [ ] Verify source and public contract guides agree on behavior, failure semantics, ownership, and limitations.
- [ ] Verify diagrams represent current contracts rather than future execution paths.
- [ ] Independently check SVG rendering and, where applicable, browser accessibility-tree exposure, keyboard interaction, and screen-reader behavior. Do not claim those checks passed without evidence.

## Known alpha.7 scope boundary to keep visible

The current kernel does not implement repository localization or content-hash verification, bootstrap-only initial composition, background localization, live deferred promotion into an existing assembly, manifest refresh, side-by-side replacement, atomic host handoff, generation leases/retirement, or serialize-then-relinquish shutdown. Collection snapshots protect collection structure, not the referenced domain-owned MicroBundle objects. Exceptions from configuration, bundle loading, or arbitration do not automatically roll back arbitrary side effects already performed.

These are explicit current limitations. They are not a reason to narrow the intended architecture to synchronous composition.

## Owner-confirmed architectural target

The intended runtime must support loading experiences and swapping active experiences while the application is running. Manifest metadata should provide the identity and dependency information needed to derive a safe loading plan; FSM_COS should ultimately coordinate dependency-aware loading, including parallel loading where dependencies permit it. The presentation layer should expose the coherent experience through the owner's moniker rather than exposing the orchestration machinery as the user experience.

This target is distinct from the current implementation. The existing schedule and load-plan types describe dependencies and track state; they do not themselves perform parallel loading, localization, live promotion, atomic experience replacement, or safe retirement of an old experience. Those capabilities require explicit runtime contracts, execution coordination, failure/cancellation semantics, and tests before they can be claimed as implemented. The workshop editor's current limitations must not be treated as a ceiling on the runtime architecture.


## Publication authorization is separate

- [ ] Obtain explicit owner authorization before publication.
- [ ] Verify the intended stable source commit and exact public-dependency artifact.
- [ ] Only then revisit the disabled publish guard and workflow dispatch path.
- [ ] After an authorized publication, verify the exact version on NuGet and record the source SHA, workflow run, and artifact hash.

Do not assign a readiness percentage from this checklist until each applicable gate has current evidence for the same candidate SHA.
